data.title: New York Times upgraded to Buy at Guggenheim on digital growth, valuation
data.description:
Guggenheim upgraded The New York Times Company (NYT) to Buy from Neutral and raised its price target to $82 from $70, citing a more attractive valuation and confidence in sustained digital advertising and subscription growth.

New PT represents about 16.6% upside from the stock's last close.

Analyst Michael Morris and team said the company can sustain “low-double digit digital advertising growth” through 2027 despite tougher comparisons, citing strong demand across its News, Sports, Games, and Shopping properties, as well as additional inventory and video monetization opportunities.

Morris expects digital subscriptions to grow about 10% next year, supported by higher average revenue per user and more than 1.09 million net additions. It said the company has “enough levers to pull” to sustain ARPU growth despite a tough comparison following a $5 price increase for its most tenured bundled subscribers this year.

Operating expenses are also expected to normalize to “mid-single digit” growth as the company laps investments in video and newsroom initiatives, though elevated sales and marketing spending remains a concern.

The brokerage raised its 2027 adjusted operating profit forecast to $714 million from $682 million, above the consensus of $699 million, and said NYT’s valuation now offers an “attractive entry point.”

Shares edged about 1.5% higher in the premarket trading on Tuesday.

data.title: Honeywell upgrades Marine Corps security; labor cost seen down 80%
data.description:
• Honeywell Technologies (HON) announced on Tuesday that it successfully deployed its LenelS2 OnGuard access control system for the U.S. Marine Corps, supporting its Barracks 2030 modernization initiative.
  • The platform enables remote management of access permissions and activity monitoring across participating barracks, replacing fragmented legacy systems.
  • The platform is designed to support more than 70K locks across Marine Corps installations.
  • The modernization effort is estimated to reduce labor costs by ~80% and material costs by 60% compared with legacy systems.
  • The pilot at Marine Corps Air Station Beaufort, South Carolina, met its objectives ahead of schedule, paving the way for expansion to additional locations.
  • The deployment strengthens Honeywell’s position in large-scale government security and access control projects.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Algorhythm announces CEO departure
data.description:
Algorhythm (RIME) announced on Tuesday an evaluation of strategic alternatives and a corporate repositioning.

As part of the transition, the company dismissed Gary Atkinson as chief executive officer, following approximately 20 years of service. Atkinson also resigned from the company’s board of directors.

“I want to take this opportunity to thank the many employees, business partners, customers, and shareholders who have supported the Company throughout my time here,” said Gary Atkinson. “I am proud of what our team has accomplished together and believe we have positioned Algorhythm for an exciting new chapter.”

“This transition was part of a deliberate process by the Company to position itself for its next phase of growth,” continued Atkinson. “I am excited about the opportunities being pursued by the Company and believe the new leadership team brings a compelling vision for its future. As a continuing shareholder, I look forward to watching that strategy take shape in the coming weeks and months.”

Shares of RIME gained more than 5% pre-market. 

Source: press release

data.title: Santos signs deals to buy Canadian LNG, sell to South Korea
data.description:
Santos (STOSF) (SSLZY) said Tuesday it signed a ​liquefied natural gas supply agreement with South Korean steelmaker ‌POSCO (PKX) and a purchase agreement with Canada's Western LNG; financial terms were not disclosed.

Santos (STOSF) (SSLZY) said it agreed to key commercial terms with POSCO (PKX) for a 10-year supply of LNG sourced from Santos' diversified global LNG portfolio on a delivered ex-ship basis, with supply starting in 2030 or 2031.

The Australian company also entered into a heads of agreement with Western LNG to purchase ~1M metric tons/year of LNG from the proposed Ksi Lisims LNG project in British Columbia on a free on board basis for up to 20 years from around 2031.

Ksi Lisims is a proposed 12M tons/year floating LNG export project on land owned by the Nisga'a Nation.

data.title: Driven Brands updates on capital allocation priorities
data.description:
Driven Brands Holdings (DRVN) announced updated capital allocation priorities aimed at accelerating growth and driving long-term shareholder returns.

Key capital allocation priorities will include continuing to invest in Take 5 growth, leveraging its proven operating model, strong 4-wall economics, and compelling cash-on-cash returns. The growth is anticipated to come through units in new and existing markets and may include acquisitions where attractive. Driven Brands (DRVN) set a long-term net leverage target of 2X to 3X net debt to adjusted EBITDA. The range was said to balance financial flexibility, investment capacity, and efficient use of capital while maintaining a strong balance sheet.

Returning capital to shareholders will also be a priority, beginning with a $100M share repurchase authorization.

"The strength of Driven Brand’s Growth and Cash framework has been on full display over the last several years as Driven reduced its net leverage from 5.0x at the end of 2023 to an expected 3.0x at the end of Q3 2026, reaching our 3.0x target a full quarter ahead of plan," highlighted CEO Danny Rivera. He noted the company is entering a new phase focused on deploying capital to support growth, maintaining financial flexibility, and enhancing shareholder value.

Shares of Driven Brands (DRVN) gained 1.1% in the premarket session.

data.title: Cogent Bio granted third FDA review for lead asset
data.description:
Cogent Biosciences (COGT) on Tuesday announced that the FDA has accepted its marketing application for its lead candidate, bezuclastinib, for a rare form of blood cancer, marking the third indication for which the tyrosine kinase inhibitor is currently under regulatory review in the U.S.

The FDA accepted the company’s new drug application for bezuclastini in advanced systemic mastocytosis, assigning June 29, 2027, as the target action date, Cogent (COGT) said, adding that the regulator has no plans to convene an advisory committee to discuss the NDA. 

NDAs targeting bezuclastinib's use in a rare cancer known as gastrointestinal stromal tumors and a rare disorder known as nonadvanced systemic mastocytosis are also currently under FDA review, with target action dates set for November 30 and December 30, respectively.

“With an excellent commercial and medical team in place, we are excited and ready for the potential launches later this year,” Cogent (COGT) CEO Andrew Robbins remarked.

data.title: Fifth Third expects $850M of cost synergies in Q4 on Comerica acquisition
data.description:
Fifth Third (FITB) expects to achieve $850M in pre-tax run-rate cost synergies in Q4 on the back of the Comerica acquisition.

The bank said the Comerica integration is completed.

The company sees over $500M in revenue opportunities over the next three to five years.

data.title: Biodexa Pharmaceuticals enters warrant exercise transaction for $2.3M gross proceeds; shares rise
data.description:
• Biodexa Pharmaceuticals (BDRX) has entered into a warrant exercise agreement to exercise certain outstanding warrants to purchase an aggregate of 2.20M American depositary shares of the company at an exercise price of $1.05 for gross cash proceeds of ~$2.3M.
  • The exercising holder will receive new unregistered warrants to purchase an aggregate of up to 4.41M ADSs.
  • The new warrants will have an exercise price of $1.05, will be immediately exercisable upon issuance, and will have a term of exercise of five years.
  • The closing of the warrant inducement transaction is expected to occur on or about September 15, 2026.
  • BDRX shares up 18% premarket.

data.title: Amerant Bancorp prices $50M notes offering
data.description:
• Amerant Bancorp (AMTB) priced an offering of $50M senior notes due 2031, with the notes carrying a 7% annual interest rate.
  • The unsecured, unsubordinated notes will mature on Sept. 17, 2031, with interest payable semiannually on March 17 and Sept. 17 beginning in March 2027.
  • The offering is expected to close Sept. 17, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. The company intends to use the net proceeds from this offering for general corporate purposes.
